source: Shared XMP conversation and current workspace; Roger Linn primary-source research catalog; external specification review pending

stages.title: Requirements, hardware boundaries and reproducible tools
stages.outcome: A new developer can reproduce the desktop baseline while hardware access remains explicit and bounded.

substeps.title: Baseline the requirements
substeps.deliverable: Versioned requirement IDs, external specification provenance when supplied, V1 inclusions, exclusions and open decisions.

substeps.title: Reproduce the development environment
substeps.deliverable: Pinned Node/Python/native dependencies, toolchain doctor and clean-checkout CI.

substeps.title: Record upstream provenance and licences
substeps.deliverable: Pinned source commits, verified archives, component licence ledger and update review process.

substeps.title: Establish target-specific access policies
substeps.deliverable: Protected Force identity, passive inventory profile and explicit future Live Mk1 lab authorization contract.

stages.title: Executable acceptance harness and target adapters
stages.outcome: One acceptance specification can verify independent desktop, native, booted-OS and authorized USB targets with truthful reports.

substeps.title: Build scenario runners and isolated fixtures
substeps.deliverable: Cucumber bindings, deterministic fixtures, per-scenario worlds, cleanup and process exit propagation.

substeps.title: Define target adapters and capability preflight
substeps.deliverable: Typed adapters, required capabilities, fail-closed target selection and no implicit transport fallback.

substeps.title: Capture evidence and qualification results
substeps.deliverable: JUnit/JSON/HTML reports with build, fixture, profile, timing, logs, screenshots and capture provenance.

substeps.title: Integrate CI and stage completion gates
substeps.deliverable: Plan-to-test traceability, regression lane, required target matrix and failures for undefined/pending/missing evidence.

stages.title: Project model, assets and universal parameters
stages.outcome: A musician can reopen a complete project with stable track, clip, scene, asset and parameter identities.

substeps.title: Version and migrate the musical project model
substeps.deliverable: Eight independent tracks, sixteen scenes, validated references, migrations and explicit resource bounds.

substeps.title: Create the parameter registry
substeps.deliverable: Stable IDs, ranges, units, smoothing and precedence of base values, automation, locks, macros and modulation.

substeps.title: Manage portable sample assets
substeps.deliverable: Content-addressed assets, bounded decoding, relative references, missing-file resolution and portable bundles.

substeps.title: Make editing and persistence recoverable
substeps.deliverable: Transactional save, autosave, recovery snapshots and undo/redo across all project edits.

stages.title: Native audio host and deterministic transport
stages.outcome: The audio engine runs independently of the UI with bounded real-time processing and measurable output.

substeps.title: Implement the bounded native engine
substeps.deliverable: Audio graph, prepared buffers, sample ownership, voice stealing and allocation/lock instrumentation.

substeps.title: Implement the clock and event scheduler
substeps.deliverable: Sample-timestamped events, tempo changes, transport start/stop and deterministic offline/live ordering.

substeps.title: Separate UI and engine processes
substeps.deliverable: Versioned bounded IPC, command validation, backpressure, state snapshots and UI restart recovery.

substeps.title: Integrate host audio backends
substeps.deliverable: Mac/Linux audio interfaces, rate negotiation, underrun monitoring, disconnect handling and loopback measurements.

stages.title: Playable sampling, synthesis and audio capture
stages.outcome: A musician can select audio/MIDI machines per track, sample an input, build a kit, play a synth and resample the result in the Mac preview; OS/USB qualification remains separate.

substeps.title: Complete the sampler and browser
substeps.deliverable: Sixteen velocity-sensitive pads, preview, one-shot/gate/loop playback, chromatic pitch and choke groups. Playable defaults and explicitly declared velocity/pressure capabilities. Extensible audio/MIDI track-machine identities, versioned state, parameter metadata, trusted factories and unavailable-machine preservation.

substeps.title: Add non-destructive waveform editing
substeps.deliverable: Trim, crop, reverse, normalize and manual slicing with visible waveform boundaries and undo.

substeps.title: Implement the first synthesizer
substeps.deliverable: Bounded polyphonic subtractive synth, ADSR, filter, voice release, preset browser and recall.

substeps.title: Record and resample audio
substeps.deliverable: Explicit input arming, monitoring, bounded recording, internal resampling and interrupted-take recovery.

stages.title: Sequencing, expression and automation
stages.outcome: A musician can record and edit expressive patterns with predictable automation and note lifetimes.

substeps.title: Complete step and real-time note entry
substeps.deliverable: Sixteen to sixty-four steps, polyphonic notes, note lengths, quantization, duplicate/copy and recording. Preserve original timestamps and velocity; reversible timing correction and pressure-aware clocked note repeat with fixed-velocity fallback.

substeps.title: Add groove and per-step variation
substeps.deliverable: Swing, microtiming, seeded probability and explicit conditional-trigger semantics. Musical swing ratios with exact triplets, reversible take rendering and acknowledged native boundary changes without clock restart.

substeps.title: Add parameter locks and modulation
substeps.deliverable: Per-step locks, defined release/reset rules, LFO/macros and parameter-source precedence.

substeps.title: Record and edit automation
substeps.deliverable: Touch/latch/write modes, automation lanes, undo and transport-safe note/automation reset.

stages.title: Scenes, arrangement and live performance
stages.outcome: A complete eight-track, sixteen-scene song can be composed, performed, saved and replayed.

substeps.title: Launch independent clips and scenes
substeps.deliverable: Eight-track scene grid, queued launch/cancel, clip-relative start and explicit empty-slot behavior.

substeps.title: Build scene chains and song mode
substeps.deliverable: Scene order, repeat counts, pattern lengths, reliable transitions and song position recall.

substeps.title: Add performance controls
substeps.deliverable: Mute/solo, macro assignments, note cleanup and predictable tail behavior during transitions.

substeps.title: Complete touch and hardware-oriented workflows
substeps.deliverable: Seven-inch layouts, consistent pad/encoder/transport mappings, focus behavior and accessible error recovery. Contextual Help with focus recovery and no project/transport mutation.

stages.title: Mixing, effects, MIDI and exchange
stages.outcome: A musician can mix a song, synchronize external equipment and export audio and MIDI without state loss.

substeps.title: Build the mixer and routing graph
substeps.deliverable: Volume/pan, two inserts per track, two shared sends, master bus, metering and route validation.

substeps.title: Implement the V1 effect set
substeps.deliverable: EQ/filter/delay/reverb/distortion/compressor, presets, bypass behavior and bounded processing costs. Playable rhythmic presets with clock-synchronized divisions, explicit phase and clock-loss policies.

substeps.title: Integrate MIDI ports and clock
substeps.deliverable: Explicit port routing, input/output, transport/clock sync, reconnect and stuck-note recovery on approved fixtures.

substeps.title: Export portable audio and MIDI
substeps.deliverable: Stereo song/scene WAV and MIDI files with timing, tails, overwrite handling and round-trip checks.

stages.title: Community SDK, packages and application isolation
stages.outcome: A developer can build, test, package and install an original instrument without rebuilding the OS.

substeps.title: Stabilize application and DSP contracts
substeps.deliverable: Versioned TypeScript/native APIs, manifests, parameter metadata and compatibility negotiation. Stable note identity and negotiated optional per-note expression, without implying MIDI/MPE conformance. Extend the P05 machine envelope with reviewed native/VST/CV/input-bus host adapters and explicit isolation/compatibility contracts.

substeps.title: Ship examples and local developer tools
substeps.deliverable: Instrument/effect templates, simulator previews, build/package commands, docs and AI coding guidance.

substeps.title: Validate and manage packages
substeps.deliverable: Integrity, ABI/dependency/licence checks, project-aware upgrades and transactional package rollback.

substeps.title: Contain application failures
substeps.deliverable: UI process isolation, least-privilege capabilities, resource limits and a documented trusted-native-plugin policy.

stages.title: Standalone bootable XMP operating system
stages.outcome: XMP boots and makes music without a development server, network connection or attached computer.

substeps.title: Choose the Linux distribution and reproducible image pipeline
substeps.deliverable: Architecture-specific rootfs, pinned recipes, source/SBOM manifests and vendor-component inventory.

substeps.title: Implement boot and service lifecycle
substeps.deliverable: Audio/application startup, persistent data layout, watchdogs, clean shutdown and boot diagnostics. A playable default kit and first-beat journey without setup wizards, measured on the booted image.

substeps.title: Qualify the image in an emulator
substeps.deliverable: Generic QEMU machine, virtual audio/control adapters, headless tests, UI tests and fault-injection snapshots.

substeps.title: Package offline operation and diagnostics
substeps.deliverable: On-image content/SDK metadata, offline projects, optional disabled-by-default lab agent and local diagnostic export.

stages.title: Live Mk1 bring-up and USB-connected hardware tests
stages.outcome: A specifically authorized Live Mk1 running deployed XMP can be qualified from the computer over USB and keep playing when disconnected.

substeps.title: Prove the device, boot and recovery prerequisites
substeps.deliverable: Exact model/firmware mapping, stock-hardware evidence, recovery plan and supported USB topology; Force remains inventory-only.

substeps.title: Integrate Live Mk1 hardware adapters
substeps.deliverable: Verified internal audio, pad velocity, touch, encoders, transport, MIDI, battery and storage adapters. Qualify optional sensor dimensions individually rather than inferring pressure or gesture support.

substeps.title: Deploy an opt-in lab agent and authenticated USB transport
substeps.deliverable: Reviewed device-specific deployment followed by an isolated USB link, target/build attestation, typed commands and bounded fixture storage.

substeps.title: Run hardware qualification and USB failure tests
substeps.deliverable: Shared musical contracts, actual control/audio measurements, disconnect/reconnect, target-swap prevention and standalone operation checks.

stages.title: Reliability, recovery, updates and V1 release
stages.outcome: An independently reproducible V1 release has passing standalone and hardware evidence and a recoverable update path.

substeps.title: Qualify performance and long sessions
substeps.deliverable: Declared workload, eight-hour soak, latency/jitter/memory budgets and measured overload behavior.

substeps.title: Test project and system recovery
substeps.deliverable: VM fault injection, corrupt-data handling, restore drills and any separately authorized hardware recovery rehearsal.

substeps.title: Build reversible updates and release artifacts
substeps.deliverable: Verified images/packages, compatibility checks and transactional update/rollback suited to the verified boot layout.

substeps.title: Complete musician and developer release journeys
substeps.deliverable: Offline install/create/perform/save/export/module-install journeys, documentation and a signed-off evidence/redistribution checklist.

instrumentDesign.status: Design input and explicitly planned capability requirements; no hardware or MPE qualification
